intro.label: See my work
intro.title: Setups that shipped.
intro.lede: Six jobs, sorted by the kind of problem they were solving. Screenshots go up as I get permission to share them.

items.title: Multi server network core
items.summary: Four servers behind one address, sharing permissions, chat and player data. Each gamemode runs isolated, so a crash on minigames never touches survival, and rolling restarts mean nobody gets kicked for a server cycle.

items.title: Permission tree rebuild
items.summary: Ninety tangled permission groups cut down to fourteen inherited tracks in one weekend. The old setup granted permissions per user with no inheritance, so every promotion meant hand editing about forty nodes. Now it's one command.

items.title: Discord community structure
items.summary: A 40 channel layout with staged access that took a community from 400 to 12,000 members. New members land in six channels, and the rest opens up as they verify and take part, which keeps the first impression readable.

items.title: Closed loop server economy
items.summary: Shops, jobs and a player market balanced so money actually leaves the economy again. Server economies usually inflate because currency comes in faster than it goes out, so every income source here is paired with a sink.

items.title: Moderation and staff systems
items.summary: Hiring rubrics, shift rotas and an escalation ladder for an eleven person team spread across three timezones. The technical side was easy. The real work was writing rules clear enough that a new moderator knows what to do on their first shift.

items.title: Performance and stability pass
items.summary: A plugin audit and tuning job that took average tick time from 41ms down to 12ms. Nine plugins removed, four replaced, chunk loading and entity limits retuned. No hardware upgrade needed, because the hardware was never the problem.
